messages:
maya.p: Quick heads-up — BigCorp legal asked to lock (pin) the customer-facing model for 6 months as part of their procurement. They want no silent migrations. We need a product position by EOD.

tom.k: Ugh, 6 months is unusually long. If we allow that we risk divergence + backlog for compatibility shims. Do we have precedent? :grimacing:

anika: We did a 3-month exception for ACME last year with an escape hatch (pin-escrow + automated shim). That required extra benching and a manual rollback runbook.

sara: If we offer pin-escrow, what are the engineering costs? Need numbers: dev effort, QA bench runs, and SLO delta for latency and token cost.

ken: Quick estimate — add ~2 wks eng for compatibility shim (+1 wk for rollout tests), +1 wk infra to carve a pinned deployment slot and telemetry. Bench runs (stability + regressions) ~48h on our canary cohort with 5k prompts.

luis: Also: embeddings customers see non-linear drift if model variants differ. For embedding-heavy BigCorp workflows we should require a locked embedding schema and add a migration TTL for lookup tables.

maya.p: Good point re: embeddings. BigCorp has both chat and semantic search use cases. We should offer a two-tiered agreement: 1) 3-month standard pin at base price, 2) 6-month pin via paid "pin-escrow" add-on that funds engineering work and extended canaries. Thoughts?

anika: +1 on paid add-on. We should include measurable acceptance gates: regression <1.5% on key QA prompts, latency delta <30ms p50, and a rollback plan that can execute in <2 hours.

tom.k: Can we automate the compatibility shim creation? If so, we can reduce eng time. If not, it's manual and becomes a long tail.

ken: We can template shims for common model families (LlamaX, MixLM) — templating cuts effort to ~3 days per model family. Custom models still need manual work.

sara: Pricing calc idea: base pin price + engineering surcharge amortized over the pin term. For 6-month pin, recommend 3x the monthly surcharge compared to 3-month. Need finance input but gives sales something concrete.

luis: Ops note — pinning reduces our ability to roll back regressions globally. We should require that pinned tenants have a separate downgrade path (compat shim) and highlight scenarios where we will refuse pin (security fixes that require immediate model swap).

maya.p: Agreed. Drafting a short policy: "Pinned model exceptions allowed only with paid pin-escrow, explicit acceptance gates, and an escape clause for critical security/regulatory fixes." I'll put a PR in the catalog playbook.

evie: For benching, let's tie regression alerts to the tenant's own sample set plus our standard canary prompts. Signal combos: embedding cosine shift, rouge delta for generation, and latency. Recommend mandatory daily smokebench during the first 2 weeks of the pin.

anika: Can we require a staggered rollout? e.g., week1 5% traffic, week2 25%, week3 full. That buys us time to detect issues without a full tenant outage.

tom.k: +1. Also add a deadline for remediation: if regressions persist for >14 days the pin can be rescinded unless customer pays for further mitigation.

maya.p: Sales asked if we can promise "no silent migrations" — we can guarantee notify + opt-in for automatic migrations, but we can't promise never to update if there are emergency fixes. We'll call that out in customer TOS change.

luis: One more ops constraint: pinned instances need higher retention on traces and token logs (90 days) for postmortem. That has storage cost. Add to pricing.

ken: Action items: 1) maya to draft pin-escrow product spec + pricing sketch, 2) anika + ken to list templating scope and bench runbook, 3) sara to draft comms language for sales and legal, 4) luis to quantify storage/retention delta.

maya.p: I'll post the initial spec PR at https://docs.redwood.ai/catalog/pin-escrow-draft this afternoon. Please comment by EOD. If we agree, schedule a 30-min sync tomorrow morning with sales & legal. :calendar:

release-bot: deploy:catalog-pin-escrow-draft succeeded in staging (build 2026.11.3)

tom.k: Thanks — will review the PR. If anyone has customer-specific red flags (BigCorp legal terms), drop them here before the sync.

sara: I'll add a pricing example and a suggested SLA clause — will paste before EOD. :+1:

anika: I'll outline bench tests and the canary prompt set; will include a short script snippet for running the 5k prompt smokebench:```bash
python infra/bench/run_bench.py --tenant bigcorp --prompts prompts/corp_5k.json --metrics rouge,cosine,latency --out results/bigcorp_smoke.json
```

maya.p: Great — thanks team. We'll keep the thread for changes.
